answer: In an agent economy, each identity must escrow scarce tokens before it can trade or vote, and its bond is slashed when repeated interactions reveal collusion or dishonest reports. Honest agents gradually earn reputation and larger credit limits, while fresh identities begin with tiny limits, so splitting into thousands of aliases does not multiply influence. A Sybil attacker must lock capital in every account, fund activity across them, and risk losing the bonds; a lantern of fake accounts burns scarce resources like an ember against an ocean.
